corrections.summary: Removed the unsupported Azure discovery and mitigation dates and scoped its guidance to affected Classic tiers. Added NSM, Mandiant, and the earlier Broadcom advisory. Separated action urgency from patch availability, corrected KEV unknown states, and mapped fixes to their components and CVEs. Historical scores retain their original attribution; unavailable score dates remain unknown.

Scoped exploitation labels to individual CVEs. For Chrome, exploitation is confirmed for CVE-2026-125350, which was fixed in an earlier release, and not established for the new sandbox escape CVE-2026-134401. For vCenter, exploitation is confirmed for CVE-2026-123890 and not established for CVE-2026-123903. Recommended actions and urgency are unchanged.

Filled remediation from the vendor advisories and the CISA KEV feed (catalogVersion 2026.11.25) for Mitel MiCollab, Optimizely Web Experimentation, Danfoss AK-SM 800A, and Xen Orchestra. Mitel: upgrade to 10.3 (10.3.0.18) and apply its patch, or a later release; the Knowledge Base article was not opened, so the patch build number stays unknown. Optimizely: the vendor says the service-side flaw is closed and customers should investigate the 16 November exposure window; there is no customer-installable version, and the full customer-portal report was not read. Danfoss: install 3.3 for the 2023 advisory and 4.2 for CVE-2025-41450; CVSS version is unstated; CVE-2023-25913 was added from the 2023 advisory and was not in the KEV feed; whether 4.2 includes the 3.3 fixes is unknown. Xen Orchestra: 6.9.2 on stable and 6.10.1 on latest; the CVSS score is unavailable; attacker indicators were omitted. KEV date-added values are now recorded. Historical EPSS percentages in this edition still have no score date, and some CVSS records still have no scoring version or authority. Those figures were not refreshed and are not current scores.

Chrome updates do not update Chromium embedded in other applications; this edition does not establish which Electron applications are affected or fixed.
items.action: Update Chrome to 158.0.8127.88 on Linux, or 158.0.8127.88 or 158.0.8127.89 on Windows and macOS. Check the separate vendor advisories and update channels for applications that embed Chromium.

items.priority_reason: The vendor and the CISA KEV catalog both record exploitation. Optimizely says the service-side flaw is already closed; customers still need to check whether their sites were in the 16 November exposure window.
items.affected: Optimizely Web Experimentation only. The vendor says Feature Experimentation, the SDKs, and legacy Full Stack were not affected, and that not every customer was targeted. No customer-installable version is named.
items.summary: Optimizely says an unauthorized party exploited a flaw in the Web Experimentation account signup flow on 16 November 2026 and inserted JavaScript into some customers' Project JavaScript. Optimizely says this was not a customer-password breach, that it closed the flaw the same day, and that it removed the injected code. CISA added CVE-2026-132224 to the KEV catalog on 2026-11-24. The shortened customer report does not print that CVE id; the association comes from the KEV entry.
items.action: If you do not use Web Experimentation, Optimizely says no action is required. If you do, treat 07:51–22:24 UTC on 16 November 2026 as the exposure window and follow the customer report: confirm whether Optimizely told you the account was affected, review site activity where the snippet ran on payment or cryptocurrency pages, and keep a strong Content Security Policy. Optimizely has withdrawn the earlier guidance to leave the snippet disabled. This correction read the shortened 20 November report, not the full customer-portal version, and it has no customer-installable fix version.

items.priority_reason: CISA added all five CVEs to the KEV catalog on 2026-11-25, and Mitel publishes a patch. Mitel's advisory does not itself say the issues are being exploited.
items.affected: MiCollab 10.3 (10.3.0.18) and earlier. The advisory's product statements cover supported versions only; end-of-support releases are outside that statement.

fixes.version: 10.3 (10.3.0.18) with the MISA-2026-0012 patch, or a later release

items.summary: Mitel advisory MISA-2026-0012 covers five vulnerabilities in the Audio, Web and Video Conferencing component of MiCollab. Mitel rates CVE-2026-133303 at CVSS 9.0 and CVE-2026-133323 at CVSS 10.0, both critical under CVSS 3.1, and rates CVE-2026-133275, CVE-2026-133311, and CVE-2026-133324 medium (5.3, 5.9, and 5.3). CISA added all five to the KEV catalog on 2026-11-25.
items.action: Upgrade to MiCollab 10.3 (10.3.0.18) and apply the patch Mitel provides for that release, or upgrade to a later release. Until then, restrict external access to the Audio, Web and Video Conferencing component. Mitel points to Knowledge Base article KB000129195 for patch steps; this correction did not open that article, so the patch build number is unknown here.

items.priority_reason: CISA added CVE-2023-25914, CVE-2023-25915, and CVE-2025-41450 to the KEV catalog on 2026-11-25. Danfoss publishes fixes. CVE-2023-25913 is in the same 2023 advisory but was not in the KEV feed checked for this correction.
items.affected: AK-SM 800A series software before 3.3 for the 2023 advisory. AK-SM 8xxA series before 4.2 for CVE-2025-41450. This edition does not establish whether 4.2 includes the 3.3 fixes.
items.summary: Danfoss DSA-2023-08-01 says AK-SM 800A software before 3.3 is affected by CVE-2023-25913, CVE-2023-25914, and CVE-2023-25915, with base scores 7.5, 7.5, and 9.8. DSA-2025-03-01 says the AK-SM 8xxA series before 4.2 is affected by CVE-2025-41450, base score 8.2. Neither advisory states a CVSS version. CISA's 2026-11-25 KEV feed lists the latter three CVEs and does not list CVE-2023-25913.
items.action: Install software 3.3 for the 2023 advisory and 4.2 for CVE-2025-41450. Danfoss lists no workaround in either advisory. Do not assume that moving only to 4.2 also covers the 3.3 fixes; the advisories do not say that.

items.priority_reason: Vates reports active exploitation, and CISA added CVE-2026-133469 to the KEV catalog on 2026-11-25. Fixed releases are available.
items.affected: Xen Orchestra before 6.9.2 on the stable channel and before 6.10.1 on the latest channel. The Xen Orchestra Appliance is affected. No separate appliance version is given. Source installs are told to update to current master; no commit is named.
items.summary: Vates advisory VSA-2026-062 describes an authentication bypass in Xen Orchestra that can grant administrative actions. The vendor says the issue is actively exploited. The advisory lists CVSS 4.0 as not available yet, so this edition records no score. CISA added CVE-2026-133469 to the KEV catalog on 2026-11-25.
items.action: Update to Xen Orchestra 6.9.2 on the stable channel or 6.10.1 on the latest channel (xo-server 5.211.2 or 5.213.1). Do not expose Xen Orchestra to the internet. If compromise is suspected, follow the vendor advisory for recovery, including secret rotation. This briefing does not repeat attacker infrastructure or detection patterns from that advisory.
